original_question: Prove nonlinear stability of the Kerr black hole under perturbations, so that initial data sufficiently close to Kerr evolve in a way that remains close to a member of the Kerr family.
target_in_paper: Section 3.4, Problem P5: "Prove the stability of the Kerr black hole." ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/710276968/Unsolved-problems-in-mathematical-physics))
correct_elements: Your draft correctly identifies that the paper is aiming at the nonlinear stability problem for Kerr under small perturbations, and it also captures the nearby contextual formulation that initial data close to Kerr should evolve so as to remain close to, or track, a Kerr end state. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/710276968/Unsolved-problems-in-mathematical-physics))
missing_details: The paper places this problem explicitly in general relativity, as part of the study of asymptotic behavior for solutions of the Einstein equations in Section 3.4, "Uniqueness and stability." ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/710276968/Unsolved-problems-in-mathematical-physics))

The nearby explanatory formulation is not just "under perturbations" in the abstract: it asks whether, starting from initial data very close to that of a Kerr-Newman black hole, the evolution "track[s]" a Kerr-Newman black hole. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/710276968/Unsolved-problems-in-mathematical-physics))

The paper stresses that the unresolved issue is the full nonlinear problem, since there has already been substantial progress on the linearized problem. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/710276968/Unsolved-problems-in-mathematical-physics))

The surrounding discussion says the intended notion of stability includes decay of perturbations of Kerr (and Schwarzschild), not merely boundedness or informal closeness. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/710276968/Unsolved-problems-in-mathematical-physics))

Problem P5 itself singles out the Kerr black hole; the nearby Kerr-Newman discussion is motivation/context, so the refined question should stay centered on Kerr rather than broaden to a separate charged-black-hole theorem. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/710276968/Unsolved-problems-in-mathematical-physics))

The paper does not specify exact norms, gauges, parameter ranges, or a formal quantifier package beyond "initial data very close"; a faithful stand-alone rewrite should therefore avoid inventing such technical hypotheses. No ambient ring/field, degree, homogeneity, or nilpotency conditions are relevant here. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/710276968/Unsolved-problems-in-mathematical-physics))
refined_question: Within general relativity, prove the full nonlinear stability of the Kerr black hole: if initial data for the Einstein equations are sufficiently close to Kerr initial data, show that the resulting evolution asymptotically tracks a Kerr black hole, with perturbations of the Kerr solution decaying, thereby giving a mathematically rigorous description of Kerr dynamics under nonlinear perturbations. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/710276968/Unsolved-problems-in-mathematical-physics))
justification: The nearest official formulation to your draft is the paper's Problem P5 in Section 3.4, not the neighboring uniqueness problem or the later cosmological-constant variants. The paragraph immediately preceding P5 supplies the intended content: start from initial data very close to Kerr-Newman data and ask whether the evolution tracks such a black hole; the same context says that linearized progress exists but that the full nonlinear problem remains open, and it describes decay of Kerr perturbations as the stability goal. The rewrite therefore keeps the paper's narrow Kerr focus, makes the Einstein-equation setting explicit, and sharpens "remains close" into the paper's own tracking/decay language without adding technical assumptions the paper itself does not state. ([scribd.com](https://www.scribd.com/document/710276968/Unsolved-problems-in-mathematical-physics))
